nodes.label: SHA-256-based staleness prevention (make pdf / make pdf-check)
nodes.norm_label: sha-256-based staleness prevention (make pdf / make pdf-check)
nodes.rationale: make pdf writes a SHA-256 of the source Markdown next to the PDF; make pdf-check re-hashes and compares, and is part of make check, so committing a changed plan without rebuilding the PDF is refused. A hash is used rather than file mtimes because mtimes do not survive a git clone (every file gets the checkout time). The same hash is printed on the PDF's title page so a reader holding only the PDF can verify it against the Markdown.

nodes.rationale: Every shipped artefact (manual, internals, manpage, --help, drs.example.yaml) must answer the reader's question on its own; a plan reference may only be a trailing footnote. nodes.label: Provisioned size, never allocated -- no over-provisioning mode
nodes.norm_label: provisioned size, never allocated -- no over-provisioning mode
nodes.rationale: z_d is always the disk's provisioned size, on thin pools (Ceph RBD, LVM-thin, ZFS) exactly as on thick ones; the pool's own 'used' is display-only. Feeding 'used' into the reserve or transient check would let a plan 'fit' only while disks stay thin, which nothing bounds, so assume_thick_provisioning:false is refused on purpose and execute.py's live pre-move re-check sums provisioned size too, with no allocated-size fallback even on error.

nodes.label: ortools/CP-SAT pip-install exception in CI
nodes.rationale: ortools is a large C++ extension not packaged in Debian and not vendorable, so it must stay an optional runtime dependency (solver.backend: auto falls back to CBC then the heuristic without it). GitHub Actions pip-installs it (--break-system-packages) purely so test_optimize.py's CP-SAT-parametrized cases have something to run against in CI, after typecheck; this never touches the packaged build/install/autopkgtest path and is the one deliberate, reviewed exception to the 'apt, never pip' rule -- not a precedent for working around other missing Debian packages.

nodes.label: The three resolved black/flake8 disagreements (E203, W503, E704)
nodes.norm_label: the three resolved black/flake8 disagreements (e203, w503, e704)

nodes.label: Snapshot reserve never traded against balance
nodes.norm_label: snapshot reserve never traded against balance
nodes.rationale: used + max(f*Z_s, soft_s) <= C_s must hold; the lexicographic two-stage solve (minimise sum r_s, fix it, then optimise balance) is the default so the reserve slack can never be sacrificed for a better balance score. The single-stage big-M form is a fallback whose penalty P is computed from the group's absolute load at model-build time, never a hard-coded config value, so it cannot be under-set into ineffectiveness.

nodes.label: reserve-tradeoff.yaml fixture (reserve vs balance conflict)
nodes.rationale: fc-tier1 cannot fail the way that matters because every reserve-violating assignment there is also worse on balance, so the lexicographic and big-M solve paths agree at any penalty. reserve-tradeoff.yaml puts them in genuine conflict: the lexicographic solve leaves the group maximally imbalanced rather than breach the reserve by 1 TiB, the configured big-M penalty P=1000 agrees, but P=5 would move the disk and produce a plan the scheduler then refuses to order -- proving the lexicographic solve is the one that must be the default.

nodes.rationale: Guards against a string of individually-reasonable small commits landing straight on main, which adds up to an un-reviewable history. nodes.label: Debian-trixie-first dependency policy (rmadison check)
